scope: Documented proposed terms only; no enactment or current-force inference. Original official status assessments retained.
findings: HB1265 proposed one-year interval begins at effective date, not enactment. Section7 proposes effectiveness60days after passage. Study report contains literalNovember1,2025 and November1,2026 dates; those are not imported as operative current deadlines.
HB1722 requires both capacity20MW-or-more and primary engagement in specifiedNAICS518210 services; this establishes explicit data-center applicability.

HB1724 specifically covers anticipated generation needs for data centers requiring5MW-or-more; proposed utility transparency is explicitly data-center-related. ExactJune4 sine-die claim remains a separate source question.

HB1739 supports the recorded grid/siting/community/workforce proposals. Its credit language uses a statewide cap of20percent of total construction costs; the appended fiscal note expressly identifies ambiguity and implementation assumptions. Do not convert those assumptions into a fixed per-project entitlement.
